findings: The current page and corrected PNG show a class-F extinguisher used by staff for hot cooking fat, a protected oxygen-limitation model, and the prominent warning against water; the active public image hash matches the reviewed PNG.

The first paper/fat response-card case asks for heat removal versus an oxygen-blocking class-F agent, rejects both water and a blanket as general fat-fire advice, and asks learners to perform no firefighting. This repairs the specific prior DGUV safety defect without replacing it with learner action.

The second independent case uses supplied protected-model data and distinguishes low oxygen from inadequate temperature. It tests the same fire triangle by a different observation, with no ignition procedure. German and English demands and expected inferences agree.

The current page and corrected PNG show H2 + Cl2 to 2 HCl with separate qualitative energy-accounting cards and no depicted free-atom reaction intermediate; the active public image hash matches the reviewed PNG.

Methane combustion is atom-balanced and has correct broken and formed bond counts; supplied qualitative bars on the same reaction amount imply exothermic net release. The independent water-splitting case has the reverse energy direction and correctly avoids a claim of spontaneous reaction. Neither case requires a numerical result.

The profile correctly distinguishes energy bookkeeping from a demonstrated stepwise mechanism. Its free-atom caveat is chemically sound, although the corrected image itself no longer contains such a schematic. Both languages state the same competence and transfer limits.
